steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Configure the risk settings and mode, and keep the demo open while the live account warms up.

pros: Fast setup - minutes to a live dashboard.
Free registration and a demo account.
cons: Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
redFlags: No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.
Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.
A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.

faqs.a: The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
We scored Lys Rentevik 4.8 out of 5. The deductions come from the disclosure gaps, not the mechanics. With the US$250 minimum and the demo as guardrails, the risk stays yours to control.
